newsitem.title: EGYPT: PLO leader says Netanyahu like Hitler.
newsitem.headline: PLO leader says Netanyahu like Hitler.

text.p: PLO leader Farouk Kaddoumi on Wednesday likened Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Nazi leader Adolf Hitler and called for international sanctions to isolate Israel politically and economically.

Kaddoumi, head of the Palestine Liberation Organisation's political (foreign affairs) department, also said the Arabs were ready for a summit, possibly including Iraq, to back the Palestinians against Israeli policies.
"Netanyahu is a man who in his behaviour resembles Hitler -- in his arrogance, conceit, stubbornness and his refusal to accept any aspect of peace," Kaddoumi told reporters.
He was speaking at Cairo airport shortly before leaving for Morocco for a meeting of the Jerusalem committee on Israel's housing project or settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Asked what the Palestinians wanted from the meeting, Kaddoumi said: "We are asking for a united Arab stand... We ask ...the international community to impose a political and economic blockade on Israel, and if possible that Israel's membership (of the United Nations) be frozen, as South Africa's was in the past, for its racist practices."

Earlier on Wednesday, after a meeting with Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid, Kaddoumi told reporters the Arabs must put behind them the wounds of the Gulf War, when Arab states joined the military alliance against Iraq.
Asked if he thought an Arab summit was needed to respond to Israel, he said: "We are in favour of the Arabs speaking with one voice and adopting a united Arab position...
"Iraq must come back because it protects the eastern gate of the Arab nation and we must remove all the wounds left by this war. I believe that the Arabs are now ready for such a summit."
Egypt was host to an Arab summit in Cairo last June but it did not invite Iraq because some Gulf leaders refused to sit alongside representatives of the Iraqi government.
Libya and Syria have also said they favour an Arab summit but Egypt has not been enthusiastic.
Kaddoumi said he welcomed the outcome of an Islamic summit in Pakistan at the weekend. The summit asked Islamic states to reconsider relations with Israel.
He added that resolutions adopted at a meeting of Arab foreign ministers in Cairo next week would be "more clear".
Kaddoumi and Abdel-Meguid discussed preparations for the ministerial meeting, a twice yearly event.
